textbookText: 7. Write any four aspects to pay attention regarding variables in scientific study. Ans:- Any four aspects to pay attention regarding variables in scientific study are, 1. Clearly identify independent, dependent, and controlled variables. 2. Change only one independent variable at a time. 3. Keep controlled variables constant throughout the experiment. 4. Measure dependent variable accurately and objectively. 8. What are variables? Mention any three importance of variables in scientific study. Ans:- Variables are measurable factors in an experiment that can change or be controlled. Importance: 1. Help to test hypotheses. 2. Allow researchers to study cause–effect relationships. 3. Ensure fairness and reliability in experiments. 9. Karma connected a dry cell to a bulb using a few pieces of wire and lit the bulb. He was curious to know how the thickness of the used wire affect the life span of a dry cell. Answer the following questions based on this experiment. a) Write dependent and dependent variables with reason. Ans:- Independent variable: Thickness of wire – because Karma changes it. Dependent variable: Life span of dry cell – because it depends on wire thickness. b) Which variables should be controlled by karma? Explain. Ans:- Type of cell, type of bulb, length of wire, and environmental conditions should be controlled for fair results. c) What is the hypothesis of this experiment? Ans:- Thicker wires will allow more current to pass, which reduces the life span of the dry cell faster. 10. Subodh wanted to find out how the how the colour of an object affects its ability to hold heat. For that he took four conical flasks and coated the first flasks with with black color enamel, and second with the white enamel, the third with green enamel and the fourth with red enamel. Then, he filled all the flasks with water, closed the mouth of each flasks tightly with cork and then kept them in the sun. After some time he measured the temperature of water in each flask with the help of a thermometer and noted the readings. Answer the following questions based on this experiment. a) What is the hypothesis of this experiment? Ans:- Dark-coloured objects absorb more heat, while light-coloured objects absorb less heat when kept in sunlight. b) Identify the independent variable and dependent variable in Subodh’s experiment with reason. Ans:- Independent variable: Colour of the flask – because Subodh changes it.

Dependent variable: Temperature of water inside the flask – because it depends on colour. c) Which variables should be controlled by Subodh? Ans:- Amount of water, size and shape of flasks, exposure time to sunlight, and cork sealing must be controlled. ***
